resolutions.researcher_notes: No independent source names the 'Defa-Brega' pipeline by that name (checked GEM/SourceWatch mirrors, DDG/Bing, Arabic queries, Libya Herald/Attaqa/Al Wasat style outlets, Wayback CDX for OPEC ASB coverage of Libya pipelines) -- gem.wiki's own only cited source is a 2001 print atlas (World Energy Atlas, Petroleum Economist), not a URL and not citable. Status is inferred contextually per standing guidance (status need not be a literal token): a 2025-2026 NOC press release confirms the 'North Defa field' gas compressor was serviced and is actively feeding gas into Libya's coastal gas network (Brega is a coastal Sirte Oil Co. hub on that network), and a Wood Mackenzie report confirms Defa is a currently Waha-operated producing field in the Sirte Basin. Neither source names 'Brega' or 'pipeline' explicitly, so this is circumstantial (field-level activity implying the gas offtake line is in service), not a direct pipeline citation -- tier kept at medium rather than high. OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (recovered via Wayback: https://web.archive.org/web/20250430112638/https://www.opec.org/assets/assetdb/asb-2012.pdf, extracted with pdftotext) lists Libya's Sirte Oil-operated gas lines individually (Brega/Benghazi, Nasser/Brega, Km-91.5/Brega, Km-81.5/Brega, etc.) but contains no 'Defa' entry at all -- so the known ASB-Wayback recovery trick does not apply to this specific line and was not used as a citation.

Same two sources as Status: NOC's 2025-2026 release describes gas (not oil) flaring/compression and gas supply to the coastal network specifically at the North Defa field, and Wood Mackenzie confirms Defa as a Waha-operated Sirte Basin field. Both are field-level, not pipeline-named, so this corroborates 'associated/produced fuel is gas at Defa' rather than literally naming the Defa-Brega line's commodity. No outlet was found describing the Defa-Brega line by name, so treat as circumstantial support (medium), not a direct hit.

No source (English or Arabic) was found stating a length for a 'Defa-Brega' gas pipeline. Checked: DuckDuckGo/Bing web queries (plain and Arabic), gem.wiki/SourceWatch mirrors (read-only, not citable -- their only listed reference is a non-URL 2001 print atlas), and the OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 gas-pipeline list recovered via Wayback (https://web.archive.org/web/20250430112638/https://www.opec.org/assets/assetdb/asb-2012.pdf, pdftotext-extracted) which enumerates Libya's Sirte Oil/Waha/Zueitina/Mellitah gas lines individually by name (Brega/Benghazi 246mi, Nasser/Brega 172mi, Km-91.5/Brega 92mi, Km-81.5/Brega 82mi, etc.) -- none of these entries is named for Defa, and none converts to ~299 km (185.8 mi) closely enough to responsibly treat as the same line (nearest by diameter, Nasser/Brega at 172mi/36in, is a ~7% length mismatch and a different named field, so not asserted as equivalent). Marking UNRESOLVED rather than force a speculative match; flagging that the 299 km figure could not be corroborated or contradicted.

Wikipedia's Al Wahat District article directly confirms Brega is one of the district's towns, supporting EndLocation=Brega / EndState-Province=Al Wahat. Wood Mackenzie confirms Defa is a real, currently Waha-operated field in the Sirte Basin of eastern Libya, supporting StartLocation=Defa gas field as a genuine place, but no source independently pins Defa itself to 'Al Wahat' province by name (only Brega's district membership is directly sourced) -- flagging that the Start side of the province/district claim is not separately confirmed, only inferred from Defa's known Sirte Basin/Waha-concession location, which regionally overlaps Al Wahat District. No contradiction found.

NOC's own subsidiary-companies page lists Waha Oil Company and Sirte Oil Company (the operators active in the Defa/Brega area) as NOC subsidiaries. Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article independently confirms NOC is a Libyan state-owned enterprise (owner: Government of Libya) and states 'NOC has a network of onshore oil, gas and product pipelines,' i.e. NOC/the Libyan state is the ultimate owner of the country's onshore gas pipeline grid. Neither source names the Defa-Brega line individually or gives an exact ownership percentage, so this supports the general claim (NOC/state ownership of Libya's onshore gas transport network, encompassing Waha- and Sirte Oil-operated infrastructure) rather than a line-item-specific 100% figure; no contradicting ownership claim was found for this line.
